high.title: Tokopedia Boss Says No Layoffs, But Calls It 'Workforce Restructuring'
high.summary: Executive Director of Tokopedia and TikTok E-commerce Indonesia Stephanie Susilo denied mass layoffs (PHK) at TikTok or Tokopedia Group, describing the situation as a 'workforce restructuring.' The statement was made following a coordination meeting with the Deputy Speaker of Parliament and the Minister of Manpower, indicating the issue has reached the highest levels of government. This is significant for investors monitoring TikTok's post-acquisition integration strategy in Indonesia and its implications for the local tech labor market.

high.title: KSPI President: TikTok Must Be Held Accountable for Mass Layoffs at Tokopedia
high.summary: Indonesia's Presidential Special Advisor on Labor and KSPI President Said Iqbal is pressing TikTok to take responsibility for reported mass layoffs at Tokopedia following TikTok's acquisition of the majority stake in the e-commerce platform. Reports suggest up to 90% of Tokopedia employees may have been cut, raising serious concerns about foreign acquisitions and worker protections in Indonesia's digital economy. This controversy could trigger new regulatory scrutiny over foreign tech acquisitions and labor compliance in Indonesia.

high.title: Prabowo Appoints Danantara to Export Electricity to Singapore
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has designated BPI Danantara as the implementing body for cross-border electricity trade with Singapore, announced during a bilateral meeting with Singaporean PM Lawrence Wong. Danantara is also tasked with activities in trade, digital economy, digital ecosystems, and cybersecurity. This represents a significant expansion of Danantara's mandate and could have major implications for Indonesia's energy and investment landscape.

high.title: Indonesia and Singapore Establish Carbon Market Cooperation to Boost Green Economy
high.summary: Indonesia and Singapore signed two strategic MoUs during the Leaders' Retreat between President Prabowo and PM Lawrence Wong, covering Environmental Protection Cooperation and Carbon Credit Collaboration under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. These agreements formalize environmental protection as a key pillar of the bilateral partnership and open pathways for Indonesia's carbon market development. This is significant for investors in green economy and carbon credit sectors in Indonesia.

high.title: Four State-Owned Asset Management Companies Officially Merge Under Danantara
high.summary: Danantara (BPI) has officially merged four state-owned asset management firms — PNM Investment Management, BNI Asset Management, Mandiri Manajemen Investasi (as the surviving entity), and BRI Manajemen Investasi — into a single integrated platform. The decision was made in a meeting attended by top Danantara leadership including CEO Rosan Roeslani and COO Dony Oskaria. This consolidation aims to create Indonesia's largest asset management company, improving efficiency, governance, and investment attractiveness for state assets.

high.title: Indonesia's Plan to Export Electricity to Singapore, But Pricing Not Yet Win-Win
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has announced that Danantara (BPI) has been appointed to implement cross-border electricity trade with Singapore, following a meeting with Singaporean PM Lawrence Wong. Danantara has also been tasked with activities in trade, digital economy, digital ecosystems, and cybersecurity. However, pricing for the electricity export deal has not yet reached a mutually beneficial agreement, signaling ongoing negotiations critical to Indonesia's energy export ambitions.

high.title: Four State-Owned Asset Management Companies Officially Merge Under Danantara
high.summary: Danantara (BPI) has officially merged four state-owned asset management firms — PNM Investment Management, BNI Asset Management, Mandiri Manajemen Investasi (surviving entity), and BRI Manajemen Investasi — into a single entity. The merger aims to create Indonesia's largest asset management company with greater integrated portfolio management, improved governance, and enhanced investment attractiveness. This consolidation is a significant structural move in Indonesia's state-owned investment landscape with broad implications for capital markets.

high.title: Rupiah Weakens, Bank Indonesia Says Still Better Than Russian and Thai Currencies
high.summary: Bank Indonesia defended the Rupiah's performance, stating it remains relatively stable compared to other emerging market currencies including Russia, Thailand, Philippines, and India following the June 17 FOMC meeting. BI noted that the Russian Ruble was the worst performer, weakening 5.5% from June 17 to July 6, while the Rupiah fared comparatively better. The hawkish signals from Fed officials have driven the Dollar Index (DXY) to its highest level in a year, putting pressure on all emerging market currencies.

high.title: Bank Indonesia Reveals Root Cause of US Dollar Breaking Back Above Rp 18,000
high.summary: The Rupiah briefly touched the psychologically critical level of Rp 18,000 per US Dollar on Monday July 6, with an intraday high of Rp 18,009, before stabilizing at Rp 17,992 on Tuesday morning. Bank Indonesia attributed the volatility to hawkish signals from Fed officials following the June 17 FOMC decision to hold rates at 3.5%-3.75%, with markets now pricing in the probability of future rate hikes rather than cuts. This development poses significant risks for Indonesian businesses with USD-denominated debt and import-dependent industries.

high.title: IHSG Closes in the Green, Strengthens to Level 5,986
high.summary: Indonesia's main stock index (IHSG/JCI) closed up 1.19% or 70.42 points at 5,986.49 on Tuesday, despite brief dips into negative territory during morning trading. Market breadth was positive with 430 stocks advancing versus 212 declining, and total transaction value reached Rp 10.3 trillion involving 22.25 billion shares. The recovery signals resilient investor sentiment in the domestic equity market despite ongoing Rupiah pressure.

high.title: US Dollar Remains Comfortable at Rp 17,900 Level
high.summary: The US Dollar continued to trade at elevated levels against the Rupiah at Rp 17,992, down only marginally by 3 points (0.02%) on Tuesday morning. The Dollar showed broad weakness against major currencies including the Japanese Yen, Australian Dollar, British Pound, Euro, Singapore Dollar, and Chinese Yuan, suggesting the Rupiah's weakness is partly idiosyncratic. The persistent high USD/IDR level remains a key concern for inflation and import costs in Indonesia.

medium.title: Manpower Minister Reveals Strategy to Prevent Layoff Wave in Manufacturing Industry
medium.summary: Minister of Manpower Yassierli outlined the government's approach to preventing mass layoffs in the manufacturing sector, centered on a dedicated PHK Task Force led by the Minister of State Secretariat with an early warning system to detect at-risk sectors. This signals growing government concern over employment stability in manufacturing, a key sector for Indonesia's economy. Investors in Indonesian manufacturing companies should note the increased government oversight and potential interventions that may follow.

medium.title: 4,000 Companies Register for National Internship Program, Submit 130,000 Vacancies
medium.summary: Within one week of opening registration for the National Internship Program 2026, 4,000 companies have signed up via the MagangHub platform, proposing approximately 130,000 internship positions, though these will be verified against a 1-per-5 employee ratio rule. The government has set a first-batch quota of 50,000 interns out of a total 150,000 annual target. This initiative reflects the government's broader effort to address youth unemployment and workforce readiness amid rising layoff concerns across multiple industries.

medium.title: Unilever Plans Major Investment in North Sumatra's SEZ, Groundbreaking Next Month
medium.summary: Unilever Global is set to invest in the Sei Mangkei Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Simalungun Regency, North Sumatra, with a groundbreaking ceremony planned for next month. The investment aims to establish a global supply chain hub and global value chain center for the multinational company. This signals growing foreign investor confidence in Indonesia's SEZ infrastructure and could attract further ancillary investment to the region.

medium.title: Tokopedia Refutes Mass Layoff Claims, Says Over 100 Positions Currently Open for Recruitment
medium.summary: Amid widespread social media reports of mass layoffs at Tokopedia and TikTok Shop, Executive Director Stephanie Susilo stated the company is actively recruiting for more than 100 positions in Indonesia. The issue drew attention from parliament and the Ministry of Manpower, with a meeting held between DPR Deputy Speaker Sufmi Dasco Ahmad, TikTok representatives, and the Minister of Manpower. The clarification is relevant for market sentiment around Indonesia's e-commerce sector and labor market stability.

medium.title: Tokopedia Boss Denies Mass Layoffs, Says Employees Are Taking Voluntary Compensation Packages
medium.summary: Tokopedia and TikTok E-commerce Indonesia Executive Director Stephanie Susilo clarified that there are no layoffs (PHK) occurring at TikTok or Tokopedia Group, describing the situation instead as workforce restructuring and internal mobility. She made the statement after a coordination meeting with DPR Deputy Speaker Sufmi Dasco Ahmad and the Minister of Manpower Yassierli. This is relevant for investors monitoring employment trends at major Indonesian tech and e-commerce players amid ongoing sector consolidation.

medium.title: Tokopedia CEO States No Layoffs, Only Workforce Restructuring at TikTok and Tokopedia Group
medium.summary: Executive Director Stephanie Susilo reiterated after a DPR meeting that no formal layoffs are taking place within TikTok or Tokopedia Group, framing current changes as workforce reorganization. The clarification was made in response to widespread social media reports of mass job cuts. Investors in the Indonesian tech and e-commerce sector should monitor this development given its implications for workforce stability and corporate restructuring at one of Indonesia's largest digital commerce groups.

medium.title: List of 10 Industries in Indonesia Along with Their Salaries
medium.summary: Adecco Indonesia has released its 2026 Recruitment Market and Salary Trends survey covering 10 industry segments including banking & financial services, FMCG, IT & technology, mining, oil & gas, and others. The guide reflects gross monthly salaries based on experience and qualifications sourced from client and candidate data. This is relevant for businesses benchmarking compensation and for professionals assessing career opportunities across key Indonesian sectors.

medium.title: Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair Visits Danantara
medium.summary: Indonesia's sovereign wealth and state enterprise investment body, Danantara, hosted former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair and his Tony Blair Institute for Global Change to discuss international collaboration on SOE transformation, investment promotion, and national development. Key discussion topics included economic zone development, industrial downstreaming, infrastructure, digital transformation, and institutional capacity building. This signals growing international interest in Indonesia's state enterprise reform agenda and could attract further foreign investment flows.

medium.title: Transportation Discount Program for Train and Air Tickets Has Ended — Here Are the Results
medium.summary: The Indonesian government's school holiday transportation incentive program, which included up to 30% discounts on train tickets, full exemption of ASDP ferry port fees, and 100% VAT subsidies (PPN DTP) on domestic economy air tickets, concluded on July 5, 2026. The program was designed to stimulate regional economic activity by encouraging public travel during the school holiday period. The wrap-up of this fiscal stimulus is relevant for assessing short-term consumer spending trends and the transportation sector's performance.

medium.title: PNM Wins Prestigious Award for Empowering Sharia Grassroots Economy
medium.summary: PT Permodalan Nasional Madani (PNM), a state-owned micro-financing institution, received the Outstanding Collaborator in Sharia Microfinance and Economic Independence award at the Anugerah Adinata Syariah 2026 event. PNM's sharia-based financing now accounts for approximately 73% of its total portfolio, reflecting a significant shift toward Islamic finance in the ultra-micro segment. This highlights the growing scale and relevance of sharia microfinance as a key pillar of Indonesia's financial inclusion strategy.

medium.title: BULOG Ensures Rice Quality is Maintained Safely Across Eastern Indonesia
medium.summary: BULOG's President Director, Lt. Gen. (Ret.) Ahmad Rizal Ramdhani, conducted a direct inspection of rice stocks and quality at the BULOG Argapura Warehouse Complex in Jayapura, Papua, including physical checks, moisture content testing, and broken grain percentage assessments. The visit underscores BULOG's commitment to maintaining national food security standards from storage to distribution, even in remote eastern regions. This is relevant for monitoring Indonesia's food supply chain integrity and inflationary pressures related to staple commodities.

medium.title: Tokopedia Management Denies Mass Layoffs, Says Workforce Restructuring is Underway
medium.summary: Tokopedia's Executive Director Stephanie Susilo clarified that the company is not conducting layoffs (PHK), but rather an internal workforce restructuring and mobility process within the TikTok/Tokopedia Group. The statement was made following a meeting with the Deputy Speaker of Parliament and the Minister of Manpower. This development is relevant for investors monitoring the e-commerce sector's labor and operational efficiency trends in Indonesia.

medium.title: List of Top 10 Industries in Indonesia and Their Salary Ranges
medium.summary: Adecco Indonesia has released its 2026 Recruitment Market and Salary Trends survey covering 10 industry segments including banking & financial services, FMCG, IT & technology, mining, oil & gas, and healthcare. The guide reflects gross monthly salary benchmarks based on experience and qualifications across key sectors. This data provides useful context for businesses and investors assessing labor cost competitiveness across Indonesian industries.

medium.title: OJK Imposes Rp 86.26 Billion in Fines Against 100 Capital Market Players
medium.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has issued administrative sanctions totaling Rp 86.26 billion in fines against 100 entities in the Capital Markets, Derivative Finance, and Carbon Exchange (PMDK) sector year-to-date through June 29, 2026. The enforcement action signals OJK's increased regulatory scrutiny and commitment to investor protection in the capital markets space. Market participants and listed companies should be aware of heightened compliance requirements to avoid similar penalties.
